Preincubation with cold HLA-A2.1+ AML-PBMCs completely inhibited the cytotoxic activity of the CD33 1Y2l-CD8+ CTL clone against 51Cr-labeled HLA-A2.1+ AML-PBMCs. column9: Degenerate specificity of HTLV-1-specific CD8+ T cells during viral replication in patients with HTLV-1-associated myelopathy (HAM/TSP).
column24: Human T-cell leukemia virus type I
column57: Human T-cell leukemia virus type I (Human T cell leukemia virus type 1)
column66: Human T-cell leukemia virus type I
column117: Fifty-three patients with HTLV-1-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP) who had the HLA-A-0201 haplotype and were residing in Kagoshima, an endemic area of Japan, were included in this study.
column129: The CD8+ T cell response to HTLV-1 is preferentially directed at the immunodominant HLA-A2-restricted epitope Tax 11-19. Epitope-specific CD8+ T cell frequency correlates well with proviral load and is significantly higher in HAM/TSP patients than in asymptomatic HTLV-1 + carriers. A combination of cytokine ICS and reactivity with altered peptide ligands (APL) was used to evaluate the degeneracy of T cell recognition. In patients, high T cell degeneracy correlated with low proviral load. Epitope-specific CD8+ T cells with degenerate specificity are increased during viral replication and control infection. This degeneracy was independent of avidity. Amino acid changes in the epitope occurred predominantly in the central positions and there was no accumulation of any variant epitope during the course of disease.

column129: Epitope-specific CTL clones lysed human HLA-A2 islet cells in the presence of the epitope in a dose-dependent manner. The amount of lysis varied between islet cells from different donors and was lower than observed with the epitope-pulsed JY B cell line, but was significantly higher than with human islet cells not expressing HLA-A2. Epitope-specific CTL lysis of the islet cells was inhibited by concanamycin A, which causes perforin degradation, but was not affected by anti-FasL antibody or the pan-caspase inhibitor zVAD. Preincubation of islet cells with IFN-? increased MHC class I expression and increased lysis by the CTL clones.

column117: The patient was a current intravenous drug user who had recently shared needles with a friend who was known to be HCV-seropositive and HIV-seropositive. He presented with an acute onset of malaise and jaundice. Initial laboratory investigations included alanine transaminase (ALT) 1073 U/liter, total bilirubin 8.6 mg/dl, anti-HCV–positive by ELISA, HCV RNA–positive, and HIV RNA–negative. A clinical diagnosis of acute HCV infection was made, and no specific pharmacologic treatment was advised. By 6 weeks, his symptoms had resolved and his ALT had normalized. PCR for HCV RNA became negative at 4 weeks and remained so during the 1 year of follow-up. HCV specific clones were generated by stimulating PBMCs with autologous B-LCLs infected with recombinant HCV-vaccinia viruses.

column117: A total of 37 HLA-A2-positive Hashimoto's thyroiditis patients were included in the study. Autoimmune thyroiditis was defined with the presence of positive TPO autoantibodies (35 mIU/ml) and/or Tg autoantibodies (40 mIU/ml) and optional hypoechogenicity in the thyroid sonography.
column129: The frequency of tetramer-positive cells in HLA-A2-positive Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) patients was significantly higher compared with HLA-A2-negative HT patients, HLA-A2-positive nonautoimmune goiter patients, and HLA-A2-positive healthy controls. Tetramer-positive cells were also detectable in thyroid-infiltrating T cells, and a correlation was observed between thyroid autoantibody concentration and the number of epitope-specific T cells.

column117: A total of 37 HLA-A2-positive Hashimoto's thyroiditis patients were included in the study. Autoimmune thyroiditis was defined with the presence of positive TPO autoantibodies (35 mIU/ml) and/or Tg autoantibodies (40 mIU/ml) and optional hypoechogenicity in the thyroid sonography.
column129: The frequency of tetramer-positive cells in HLA-A2-positive Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) patients was significantly higher compared with HLA-A2-negative HT patients, HLA-A2-positive nonautoimmune goiter patients, and HLA-A2-positive healthy controls. Tetramer-positive cells were also detectable in thyroid-infiltrating T cells, and a correlation was observed between thyroid autoantibody concentration and the number of epitope-specific T cells.

column129: The epitope-specific T cells reacted with HeLa target cells expressing HLA-A*0201 and loaded with the epitope.  T2 cells loaded with the epitope were also used as target cells and produced a positive response.  Transfection of target cells with prolyl oligopeptidase (POP) and aminopeptidase B (AP-B) inhibited epitope generation in the target cells and eliminated the response. The authors concluded that cytosolic peptidases primarily interfere with the generation of the epitope, whereas ER-resident aminopeptidases enhance such generation.

column117: Blood samples were collected from Ebola virus disease (EVD) patients during the outbreak in Guinea.
column129: At the time of admission, the differences in the percentage of CD8+ T cells stained with epitope/HLA-A*0201 tetramers between fatalities and survivors were not statistically significant. column117: Patients with advanced or metastatic HCC were enrolled. Eligibility criteria included: diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) on the basis of imaging modalities or histological examinations; no expectation of response to other therapies including surgery, RFA, or chemotherapy (e.g. sorafenib); an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0–1. Peptides were administered in liquid form, emulsified with incomplete Freund’s adjuvant (IFA) (Montanide ISA-51VG), via intradermal injection every 2 weeks (range of 3-13 doses/patient). (2008) Nature Med 14(12):1390-5 [PMID: 18997777]. Patient 9300868 (A2/24, B27/35), a HIV-1 infected homosexual male was first diagnosed as HIV-positive in 1993 but the duration of  his infection is unknown. He made a vigorous CTL response to the HLA-A2-restricted p17-8 epitope SLYNTVATL of  p17 Gag. Blood  taken in April 1996 was used to grow out a line of cells (CTL 868 line) which killed autologous peptide-pulsed B cell targets. Repeated attempts to generate SL9-specific T-cell clones from the 868 line by limiting dilution were unsuccessful. Therefore, phage display was used to isolate a TCR from a T-cell line that was only ~14% tetramer positive for the SL9 antigen. Flow cytometry of the starting CTL line confirmed that all SL9-tetramer+ cells in this line expressed a TCR made from the same combination of variable genes as the TCR selected from the phage library. The 868 TCR ? and ß chains were expressed and purified.
column129: The crystal structure of the epitope/HLA-A2 complex bound by the 868 TCR was determined, solved by molecular replacement.

column117: The patient TC underwent excision of a primary melanoma from the left thigh in 1989 and a palpable lymph node containing melanoma in 1991. Recurrent melanomas in the left breast and left arm were excised in 1995, and left breast and mediastinal masses appeared later in 1995. The patient was diagnosed with metastatic melanoma and entered into a clinical protocol. On December 22, 1995, and January 1, 1996, the patient received the s.c. injection of 10^8 PFU of a recombinant adenovirus encoding the melanoma Ag recognized by T cells 1 (MART-1). Partial regression of the mediastinal and breast melanoma metastases was observed and after two more injections in 1996, all of her disease regressed and she has remained continuously disease-free as of October 2001. The PBLs used for the present studies were obtained on January 17, 1996, 26 days after her first injection of recombinant adenovirus. T cells were expanded in vitro and cloned. Subclone 10-B5 recognized several HLA-A2+, but not HLA-A2- melanoma cell lines, and did not recognize known melanoma tumor antigens (MART-1, gp100, tyrosinase, tyrosinase-related protein (TRP)1, TRP2, MAGE-1, or NY-ESO-1).
column129: The 10-B5 clone responded to T2 cells pulsed with the epitope. The epitope sequence was from an alternative open reading frame of the BING-4 cDNA clone that started with a methionine codon and that encoded a minimum of 9 aa and conformed to an extended HLA-A2 Ag-binding motif. Clone 10-B5 responded more weakly to the 10mer peptide MCQWGRLWQL. Substitution of Cys at position 2 with Met or Leu did not improve the response.

column9: Identification of BING-4 cancer antigen translated from an alternative open reading frame of a gene in the extended MHC class II region using lymphocytes from a patient with a durable complete regression following immunotherapy.
column28: The epitope sequence is from an alternative open reading frame in the BING-4 mRNA (WD REPEAT-CONTAINING PROTEIN 46; WDR46). The BING-4 gene is located in the extended region of the class II MHC. The epitope sequence contains substitution Q2M at position 2.
column30: Fragment of a Natural Sequence Molecule
column117: The patient TC underwent excision of a primary melanoma from the left thigh in 1989 and a palpable lymph node containing melanoma in 1991. Recurrent melanomas in the left breast and left arm were excised in 1995, and left breast and mediastinal masses appeared later in 1995. The patient was diagnosed with metastatic melanoma and entered into a clinical protocol. On December 22, 1995, and January 1, 1996, the patient received the s.c. injection of 10^8 PFU of a recombinant adenovirus encoding the melanoma Ag recognized by T cells 1 (MART-1). Partial regression of the mediastinal and breast melanoma metastases was observed and after two more injections in 1996, all of her disease regressed and she has remained continuously disease-free as of October 2001. The PBLs used for the present studies were obtained on January 17, 1996, 26 days after her first injection of recombinant adenovirus. T cells were expanded in vitro and cloned. Subclone 10-B5 recognized several HLA-A2+, but not HLA-A2- melanoma cell lines, and did not recognize known melanoma tumor antigens (MART-1, gp100, tyrosinase, tyrosinase-related protein (TRP)1, TRP2, MAGE-1, or NY-ESO-1).
column129: The epitope-reactive 10-B5 clone responded to T2 cells pulsed with the native 9mer (CQWGRLWQL) or 10mer (MCQWGRLWQL) BING-4 peptide more weakly than to the epitope. The native BING-4 sequence was from an alternative open reading frame of the BING-4 cDNA clone that started with a methionine codon and that encoded a minimum of 9 aa and conformed to an extended HLA-A2 Ag-binding motif.

column117: The patient TC underwent excision of a primary melanoma from the left thigh in 1989 and a palpable lymph node containing melanoma in 1991. column117: The patient TC underwent excision of a primary melanoma from the left thigh in 1989 and a palpable lymph node containing melanoma in 1991. Recurrent melanomas in the left breast and left arm were excised in 1995, and left breast and mediastinal masses appeared later in 1995. The patient was diagnosed with metastatic melanoma and entered into a clinical protocol. On December 22, 1995, and January 1, 1996, the patient received the s.c. injection of 10^8 PFU of a recombinant adenovirus encoding the melanoma Ag recognized by T cells 1 (MART-1). Partial regression of the mediastinal and breast melanoma metastases was observed and after two more injections in 1996, all of her disease regressed and she has remained continuously disease-free as of October 2001. The PBLs used for the present studies were obtained on January 17, 1996, 26 days after her first injection of recombinant adenovirus. T cells were expanded in vitro and cloned. Subclone 10-B5 recognized several HLA-A2+, but not HLA-A2- melanoma cell lines, and did not recognize known melanoma tumor antigens (MART-1, gp100, tyrosinase, tyrosinase-related protein (TRP)1, TRP2, MAGE-1, or NY-ESO-1).
column129: The epitope-reactive 10-B5 clone responded to T2 cells pulsed with the 10mer  peptide with C2M substitution of the native 10mer (MCQWGRLWQL) BING-4 peptide more weakly than to the epitope. The native BING-4 sequence was from an alternative open reading frame of the BING-4 cDNA clone that started with a methionine codon and that encoded a minimum of 9 aa and conformed to an extended HLA-A2 Ag-binding motif.

column117: CD8+ T-lymphocytes were isolated from blood and stimulated with peptide using T2 cells as antigen-presenting cells.
column129: After isolation and stimulation, CD8+ T-cells were tested in a tetramer binding assay and further analyzed using monoclonal antibodies specific for various families of the T-cell receptor beta variable chain. Heatmap analysis shows that TRBV usage differed between young (18 to 22 years)  and older (> 60 years) donors in EBV-specific responses either when frequency was directly compared between the groups or if the hierarchy of TRBV usage within the group was examined. A single TRBV family, BV19, dominated IAV-M1-specific responses in both young and older donors. Also, CD8+ T-cells were tested in a tetramer sorting and sequencing assay. Significant differences were found in the number of glycines (Ai-v, number of nucleotide additions (Bi-v), and number of nucleotides per amino acids (Ci-v) between young and older adults and between the epitope specific and cross-reactive responses for TRAV and TRBV. Significant differences in TRAV and TRBV CDR3 lengths and family usage were observed between young and older donors.

column117: CD8+ T-lymphocytes were isolated from blood and stimulated with peptide using T2 cells as antigen-presenting cells.
column129: After isolation and stimulation, CD8+ T-cells were tested in a tetramer binding assay and further analyzed using monoclonal antibodies specific for various families of the T-cell receptor beta variable chain. Heatmap analysis shows that TRBV usage differed between young (18 to 22 years)  and older (> 60 years) donors in EBV-specific responses either when frequency was directly compared between the groups or if the hierarchy of TRBV usage within the group was examined. A single TRBV family, BV19, dominated IAV-M1-specific responses in both young and older donors. Also, CD8+ T-cells were tested in a tetramer sorting and sequencing assay. Significant differences were found in the number of glycines (Ai-v, number of nucleotide additions (Bi-v), and number of nucleotides per amino acids (Ci-v) between young and older adults and between the epitope specific and cross-reactive responses for TRAV and TRBV. Significant differences in TRAV and TRBV CDR3 lengths and family usage were observed between young and older donors.

column117: A cohort of stage IV metastatic melanoma patients who had been treated with autologous in vitro-expanded tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) were studied. Patients who had received prior anti-PD-1 immunotherapy or genetically engineered T cell or TCR therapies were excluded. The phenotypic differences that could distinguish patient adoptive cell therapy (ACT) infusion products (I.P.) administered to patients who had complete response to therapy (complete responders, CRs) from those whose disease progressed following ACT (non-responders, NRs) were analyzed.
column129: TILs in the adoptive cell therapy (ACT) infusion products (I.P) were stained with epitope tetramers. The epitope-specific TILs largely existed in the CD39+CD69+ differentiated state. However, the frequency of neoantigen-specific CD39-CD69- cells was significantly higher in complete responder (CR) I.P.  than in non-responder (NR) I.P. CD39 as a single marker indicated that CD39+ neoantigen-reactive TILs were significantly lower in CR TILs relative to NR TILs. These results indicate that at least in the context of melanoma ACT, not all CD39-negative (CD39-) TILs are bystander T cells, and that responders retain a detectable proportion of tumor-reactive TILs in a CD39- stem-like state.

column117: Patients were diagnosed with Stage IIB, III or IV colon cancer or Stage II-IV rectal cancer, and HLA-type A2 or A3. Primary tumors were examined for Her2 or CEA expression by immunohistochemistry, and patients whose primary tumors did not express Her2 or CEA were excluded. Patients were required to have completed all chemotherapy, immune therapy or radiation treatments >30 days prior to study enrollment. Participants underwent weekly vaccination for 3 weeks with CEA peptide + Her2 peptide + Tetanus helper peptide + GMCSF + Montanide ISA 51 on days 1, 8 and 15, administered intradermally and subcutaneously at two sites simultaneously. Peripheral blood was collected prior to first vaccination and at Day 1, 8, 15 and 22, then at Week 10 and Months 6, 12 and 24. The vaccine-draining lymph node (SIN) was excised 1 week after the third vaccination (Day 22) for assay.
column129: Among the eight HLA-A2+ participants, responses were observed to the epitope, CEA 571-579, in five participants.

column117: The A2-restricted epitope-specific 1G4 CTL was derived from a melanoma patient [PMID: 15837811] and [PMID: 9432985]. CTL were established by stimulation of autologous PBLs by NY-ESO-1-positive tumor cell lines established from tumor tissue obtained from an inguinal lymph node metastasis by needle biopsy. Approximately 7 to 14 days after being immunized with the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, patients underwent steady-state apheresis for T-cell collection. column117: The A2-restricted epitope-specific 1G4 CTL was derived from a melanoma patient as described in the cited reference: Jager et al. (1988) J Exp Med 187: 265-270 [PMID: 9432985]. CTL were established by stimulation of the patient's PBLs with autologous NY-ESO-1-positive tumor-derived cell lines. The 1G4 TCR was cloned, and used to transfect CD8+ or CD4+ T cell populations from PBMCs previously activated with OKT-3 anti-CD3 Ab for 5 to 21 days. Single and double amino acid substitutions were included in the CDRs by PCR. Jurkat-Dual cells were transduced with NY-ESO-1 TCR and artificial T cell-activating adapter molecules (ATAM). ATAMs were generated by inserting the intracellular domain (ICD) of activating T-cell signaling moieties into CD3z. ATAMs with the ICD of either CD28 or 4-1BB were generated, assembled into the TCR complex as a part of CD3z, and enhanced downstream signaling from the supramolecular activation cluster.
column129: Activation was measured by alterations in NF-kB signaling measuring luciferase activity after HLA-A2/epitope–specific antigen stimulation. Transduction with artificial T cell-activating adapter molecules (CD3z or CD3z/CD28) increased NF-kB signaling, with peak activity observed at 24 hours, whereas CD3z/4-1BB transduction resulted in smaller, but constant, increases in NF-kB signaling.

column117: PBMCs were obtained from patients with advanced biliary tract cancer (aBTC) after the 6th and 12th vaccine treatment with personalized peptide vaccination (PPV) with or without low dose cyclophosphamide (CPA). All patients enrolled in the study had failed at least one regimen of standard chemotherapies at the time of entry. For PPV treatment, two to four peptides were selected every cycle of six vaccinations by the levels of IgG titers speci?c to HLA-matched 31 candidate peptides. The numbers of vaccinated peptides were four, three, and two for 23, one, and zero patients in the PPV/CPA or 23, one, and one in the PPV alone, respectively. Peptides were mixed with incomplete Freund’s adjuvant (Montanide ISA-51VG; Seppic, Paris, France) and injected subcutaneously into the inguinal, abdominal, or lateral thigh areas as 1.5 mL emulsion (3 mg/each peptide). Patients received six times of PPV at 1 week intervals (the ?rst cycle) and six times at 2-week intervals (the second cycle and thereafter) until withdrawal of consent or unacceptable toxicity. In the PPV/CPA arm, patients were administered orally with 100 mg of CPA (50 mg 9 2/day) for 7 days followed by the ?rst cycle of vaccinations, and also for 7 days followed by the second cycle of vaccinations.

column117: The A2-restricted epitope-specific 1G4 CTL was derived from a melanoma patient as described in [PMID: 9432985]. CTLs were established by stimulation of the patient's PBLs with autologous NY-ESO-1-positive tumor-derived cell lines. TCRs were cloned and viral particles packaged with TCR-encoded genes were transduced T cells. TCR, termed 1G4-alpha95:LY, contained two amino acid substitutions in the third complementarity determining region of the native 1G4TCRalpha chain that conferred to CD8+ and CD4+ T cells an enhanced ability to recognize HLAA* 0201-positive target cells expressing the ESO-1antigen. The epitope-specific TCR was adoptively transferred into HLA-A:0201+ patients with NY-ESO-1+ metastatic synovial cell sarcomas or patients with metastatic melanoma.

column9: A pilot trial using lymphocytes genetically engineered with an NY-ESO-1-reactive T-cell receptor: long-term follow-up and correlates with response.
column117: The A2-restricted epitope-specific 1G4 CTL was derived from a melanoma patient as described in [PMID: 9432985]. CTLs were established by stimulation of the patient's PBLs with autologous NY-ESO-1-positive tumor-derived cell lines. TCRs were cloned and viral particles packaged with TCR-encoded genes were transduced T cells. TCR, termed 1G4-alpha95:LY, contained two amino acid substitutions in the third complementarity determining region of the native 1G4TCRalpha chain that conferred to CD8+ and CD4+ T cells an enhanced ability to recognize HLAA* 0201-positive target cells expressing the ESO-1antigen. The epitope-specific TCR was adoptively transferred into HLA-A:0201+ patients with NY-ESO-1+ metastatic synovial cell sarcomas or patients with metastatic melanoma.

column117: Patients with a wide range of advanced solid tumors were enrolled in a clinical trial of vaccine EMD640744, a cocktail of ?ve HLA class I-binding survivin peptides in Montanide® ISA 51 VG. Subjects were allocated to one of the 3 doses of the treatment (30, 100, or 300 µg peptide). Treatment was planned for 11-week initiation therapy (8 treatments), followed by 13-week maintenance therapy (4 weekly treatments). The primary end-point was immune response as assessed by ELISpot before and until week 17 after the beginning of the study treatment. The patients had colorectal cancer and were assigned to the 100 µg or 300 µg treatment group. PBMCs were tested directly ex vivo or were stimulated with the epitope or EMD640744 peptide mix for 12-14 days in vitro.
